pilate-stone.title: The Pilate Stone
pilate-stone.caption: AD 26–36 · 1961 · reused as a stair step in the Roman theater at Caesarea Maritima
pilate-stone.alt: Reconstruction plate for The Pilate Stone
pilate-stone.summary: The Pilate Stone. An Italian expedition led by Antonio Frova found the block where fourth-century builders had recycled it as a step. It is the earliest physical witness to the governor who, in Tacitus and the gospels alike, sentenced Jesus — and it quietly corrects Tacitus, who called Pilate “procurator”: the stone says prefect.

caiaphas-ossuary.title: The Caiaphas Ossuary
caiaphas-ossuary.caption: 1st century AD (c. 20–60) · 1990 · a burial cave broken open during park construction in the Peace Forest, south Jerusalem
caiaphas-ossuary.alt: Reconstruction plate for The Caiaphas Ossuary
caiaphas-ossuary.summary: The Caiaphas Ossuary. The identification is probable, not proven, and scholars have said so plainly: the spelling is not a perfect match for “Caiaphas,” the inscription carries no title, and the tomb is modest for a high-priestly family. Supporters answer with the ornate box and the match of name and age. This page keeps it at “probable.”

yehohanan-heel.title: The heel bone of Yehohanan
yehohanan-heel.caption: 1st century AD, before 70 · 1968 · a tomb opened by construction work at Giv’at ha-Mivtar, north-east Jerusalem
yehohanan-heel.alt: Reconstruction plate for The heel bone of Yehohanan
yehohanan-heel.summary: The heel bone of Yehohanan. An 11.5 cm nail had bent against a knot in the olive wood and could not be pulled out, so it was buried with him. The corrected analysis (Zias & Sekeles, 1985) reads one heel nailed and the arms likely tied. For half a century this was the only skeletal evidence of crucifixion found anywhere — and it answers, in bone, the claim that crucified men were never given burial.

galilee-boat.title: The Galilee Boat
galilee-boat.caption: c. 50 BC – AD 50 (radiocarbon and pottery) · 1986 · the exposed lakebed near Kibbutz Ginosar, during a drought, by two fishermen brothers
galilee-boat.alt: Reconstruction plate for The Galilee Boat
galilee-boat.summary: The Galilee Boat. Cedar planking on oak frames with ten different woods worked in — repaired again and again, finally stripped and scuttled. Nothing connects this boat to Jesus or any disciple, and this page makes no such claim. What it fixes is the setting: the working world of Peter, Andrew, James, and John, at exactly their time.

capernaum-house.title: Capernaum — the house under the octagon
capernaum-house.caption: 1st-century-BC house, singled out by the mid-1st century AD · excavated from 1968 · the insula sacra at Capernaum (Corbo and Loffreda)
capernaum-house.alt: Reconstruction plate for Capernaum — the house under the octagon
capernaum-house.summary: Capernaum — the house under the octagon. That the house was Peter’s rests on the chain of veneration and on Egeria — not on a deed, and the excavators’ readings of the graffiti are contested. The white limestone synagogue beside it is 4th–5th century, but it stands on basalt foundations that may belong to the synagogue of Mark 1:21. Both attributions are argued; neither is proven.

magdala-stone.title: The Magdala synagogue and its stone
magdala-stone.caption: 1st century AD, before 70 · 2009 · a salvage dig before hotel construction at Migdal, on the Sea of Galilee
magdala-stone.alt: Reconstruction plate for The Magdala synagogue and its stone
magdala-stone.summary: The Magdala synagogue and its stone. The gospels say Jesus taught “in their synagogues throughout all Galilee,” and for a long time no first-century Galilean synagogue was known — some doubted the texts on exactly this point. Magdala, Mary Magdalene’s hometown, produced one in 2009 and a second in 2021. At the first one’s center lay a carved stone bearing a seven-branched menorah, plausibly cut by someone who had seen the real one. What the stone’s full imagery means is still argued.
